ana: Quick follow-up from the postmortem — looks like we had the same paging pattern 3x this month (flaky upstream + low thresholds). I want a short action plan: remediation owners, timelines, and a safe rollout for dedupe/threshold changes.
oncall-bot: Postmortem here: https://redwood/pm/incident-123 — includes timeline + raw alert samples.
matt: Saw the log samples. Most noise is duplicate traces with different request IDs. My initial suggestion: dedupe by `trace_id` + route, 5m suppression. That removes ~60% of duplicates in the sample set.
jess: For thresholds: can we move from static 10/min to a dynamic threshold based on 95p baseline? static is too sensitive for bursty services.
leo: @ana I can own the dedupe roll. Plan: implement rule in staging -> 48h canary (subset of teams) -> roll to prod. I'll prepare the change + test cases. ETA: PR by EOD Fri.
samir: Re: risk — we need a rollback plan if dedupe hides real incidents. Suggest: initial canary routes have an alert mirror (no paging) so we can compare. Also add a high-severity override so pages still fire if error rate above X%.
matt: Example rule snippet I prototyped (staging):
```
alert_rule {
  name: "http-5xx-dedupe-by-trace"
  dedupe_key: ["trace_id","route"]
  suppression_window: "5m"
  mirror: true
}
```
jess: Also propose a cleanup of low-signal alerts (age > 90d and < 2 occurrences) — archive or convert to metrics-only. That'll cut noise and reduce cognitive load for oncall.
